title: Improve llm req -h response
objective: Make `llm req -h` print usage and a listing of every resolvable request in the configured request directory, and make `llm req <request-name> -h` print that request's parameters with their --p- command-line form, types, defaults, constraints, and x-llm-req-parameter annotations such as file bindings, without initializing a provider.

branch.name: WI-0028-request-help
branch.rationale: Each work item is processed on its own branch.

request.text:
We require a command to list available llm req <request-name>
as well as support for llm req <request-name> -h to list parameters
required to invoke an llm request.

The goal for this work item is to have great help documentation
for llm req -h [includes resolvable request listing] and
llm req <request-name> -h [includes parameters and how to
set them via the command line along w/ annotations, such as file.

scope.name: request-listing-help
scope.description: Recognize `llm req -h` and `llm req --help` and print req usage, the resolved requests directory, every resolvable request with its description, and every unavailable request directory with its loader reason.
scope.reason: The request asks for a command that lists available `llm req <request-name>` requests.

scope.name: request-parameter-help
scope.description: Recognize `llm req <request-name> -h|--help` and print the request usage, description, every parameter path as `--p-<path> <value>`, type or allowed values, required/optional status, defaults.json parameter defaults, examples, oneOf/anyOf requirement groups, `--parameters` usage, request settings, and x-llm-req-parameter file and validation annotations.
scope.reason: The request asks for parameters, how to set them from the command line, and annotations such as file.

scope.name: help-entry-points-and-docs
scope.description: Add both help forms to `llm --help`, README.md, and SKILL.md.
scope.reason: Users and agents discover commands from top-level help and the documentation.

nonGoals.name: request-execution-behavior
nonGoals.description: Do not change how `llm req` loads, validates, or executes requests, parameter parsing outside the help positions, or provider behavior.
nonGoals.reason: This work item only adds help output.

nonGoals.name: request-contract-edit-gate
nonGoals.description: Do not edit requests/README.md, requests/decisions.md, or the bundled request assets.
nonGoals.reason: requests/README.md changes require explicit operator confirmation, and help reads the existing contract.

nonGoals.name: live-provider-checks
nonGoals.description: Do not invoke a provider or add live checks; help is provider-free.
nonGoals.reason: Help must not initialize a provider, and npm test stays provider-free.

items.name: request-listing
items.description: `llm req -h` and `llm req --help` print req usage and every resolvable request in the configured request directory.
items.reason: Users need to discover which requests exist before running one.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Both forms exit 0, write nothing to stderr, and print the req usage lines, the resolved requests directory, and every resolvable request in sorted order with its parameters-schema description (falling back to title, then "No description.").
Child directories that fail to load are listed separately under "Unavailable requests" with the loader reason; regular files and dot-directories in the requests directory are not listed.
An empty requests directory prints "No requests are available." and exits 0.
A missing or invalid request-directory configuration writes one configuration_error JSON entry to stderr, writes nothing to stdout, and exits 1.

items.name: request-parameter-help
items.description: `llm req <request-name> -h` and `--help` print the parameters required to invoke that request and how to set each one from the command line.
items.reason: The request asks for parameters, command-line usage, and annotations such as file.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Each top-level parameter is printed as `--p-<name> <value>` with its type, required or optional status, description, examples, and defaults.json parameter default when present.
x-llm-req-parameter file bindings print mode, MIME type, purpose, and name or encoding when declared; validation metadata prints that an inline validation function checks the value.
Nested object properties are printed as dotted paths, arrays show the `[<index>]` element form and that a JSON array is accepted, and enum values are listed as allowed values.
Top-level oneOf and anyOf required groups are printed as "Exactly one of" and "At least one of" constraint lines, and `--parameters <json>` usage and defaults.json request settings are printed.

A request without a parameters schema prints that it accepts no parameters, and the bundled summarize request help lists `--p-path` (file, path mode) and `--p-content` (file, content mode) with an exactly-one constraint.

items.name: help-safety-and-errors
items.description: Help is read-only and provider-free, reports unknown or invalid requests as configuration errors, and leaves non-help invocations unchanged.
items.reason: Help must be safe to run anywhere and must not change existing request behavior.

acceptanceCriteria.description: An unknown request name, an unsafe request name such as `../x`, and an invalid request bundle with -h each write one configuration_error JSON entry with the loader message to stderr, write nothing to stdout, and exit 1.

Help is recognized only as the token immediately after `req` (listing) or immediately after the request name (request help); later tokens are not validated, no provider is created, and no parameter file is read.
Invocations without a help token behave as before: existing request CLI tests pass and `llm req` with no request name still exits 2 with a usage error.

items.name: help-documentation
items.description: `llm --help`, README.md, and SKILL.md document `llm req -h` and `llm req <request-name> -h`, and requests/README.md is unchanged.
items.reason: Help forms must be discoverable, and the request contract is operator-gated.

acceptanceCriteria.description: `llm --help` output, README.md, and SKILL.md each mention both help forms, and requests/README.md is byte-identical to the baseline.

items.name: quality-gates
items.description: Repository quality gates pass and every WI-0028 test case is implemented with an SDLC-TEST-CASE trace marker.
items.reason: The work item is complete only when all test cases pass and are traceable.

acceptanceCriteria.description: `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, and `sdlc work-item validate --work-item WI-0028 --json` all exit 0, and each WI-0028 test case has a test whose name and `// SDLC-TEST-CASE:` marker carry its canonical identifier.
